_comment: Two denials, because no single one has both properties worth having.
The first is evaluated inside the enclave and leaves only an HTTP 400.
The second is evaluated at the API layer and leaves a persisted action record.
Neither is described as the other. Raw headers for the first are in 04-denial.http.

enclaveEvaluated.why: For methods Privy also broadcasts, simulation runs before policy evaluation, so an unfunded wallet fails with insufficient_funds and the artifact shows the wrong control.

error.error: RPC request denied due to policy violation

apiLayerEvaluated.why: Transfer limits need transaction simulation, which runs outside the enclave; the trade is that this path leaves a fetchable record.
apiLayerEvaluated.chain: not the registry's chain — transfers accept a fixed set of named chains and Arc is not among them, so the chain here is incidental to the policy engine being shown

error.error: RPC request denied due to policy violation

attribution.problem: The response names no rule, deliberately, so a caller cannot enumerate a denylist by probing.
attribution.answer: The control run. Same wallet, same policy, same execution, same wire: one recipient signs and one does not.
attribution.notConflated: The denial wallet carries no quorum owner. A quorum-owned wallet refuses with insufficient_correct_authorization_signatures — a real block, by a different control. An artifact that conflates two controls proves neither.

policyShape.allowRule: an explicit allow for the control recipient
policyShape.whyNotAllowEverythingElse: An empty condition list is rejected with invalid_policy_format, and the operator set has no negation — eq, in, contains, starts_with, lt, lte, gt, gte, in_condition_set. 'Allow everything else' cannot be expressed.
policyShape.whyNotInConditionSet: If a condition set is deleted, every condition referencing it evaluates false: the denylist stops blocking silently while allow rules keep passing traffic.
